change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: website_name exposes a TL0 user's website to anonymous visitors
findings.body: `website_name` is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:105-111), so the restriction that hides `website` from TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers does not apply to it. `include_website?` is generated there and returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (lines 25-31; guardian at lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60, `anonymous?` at lib/guardian.rb:42). The explicit `include_website_name` at lines 153-155 only checks `website.present?`, so an anonymous visitor receives `website_name` for a TL0 user with a website. It reaches the JSON endpoint and the preloaded HTML (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:48-55) and is rendered in the header (templates/user/user.hbs:66-73), where the span shows the host and path. Fix: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list and delete `include_website_name` at lines 153-155. That `def` runs after the `define_method` from `untrusted_attributes`, so it overwrites the restricted check. The generated method already returns false for a nil value through `present?`.
findings.originReason: The diff adds the `website_name` attribute without listing it in `untrusted_attributes`.

verification.reason: `website_name` is added to `attributes` but not to `untrusted_attributes`, so no `include_website_name?` guard calls `restrict_user_fields?`. The hand-written `include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, so the serializer never calls it at all. As a result, an anonymous viewer gets a TL0 user's `website_name`, even though `website` itself is hidden from them. The candidate's note about which method overwrites which is slightly off, because the two names differ, but the leak and the fix are both correct.

findings.title: Header label does not follow website edits on the preferences page
findings.body: Before this change the label was computed in the controller from `model.website`, so it changed as the user typed. The header stays on screen while preferences are edited: `user.hbs:206` renders `{{outlet}}` inside the same template, and `routes/preferences.js.es6:5-7` uses the same `User` object. The website input is bound to `model.website` (templates/user/preferences.hbs:158). The label is now `model.website_name`, which only `findDetails` sets (models/user.js.es6:320). `save()` (models/user.js.es6:166-217) sends `website` but reads back only `bio_excerpt`. As a result the link `href` (user.hbs:69) follows the new value while the text does not. After a save, or after clearing the website, the old label keeps showing until the user leaves and returns to the profile. Fix: update `website_name` from the save response in `save()`. This needs the PUT response to include it, which I did not verify; I did not read what the users controller `update` action renders.
findings.originReason: The base template used a controller property that was recomputed from `model.website`. The diff switched it to a static value from the server.

verification.reason: In the base, `websiteName` was a computed property on `model.website`, so the label updated as the user typed. The header now reads `model.website_name`, which only `findDetails` sets via `setProperties(json.user)`. `save()` copies back only `bio_excerpt`. The preferences route reuses the same user model, and the header is rendered above the `{{outlet}}`, so the label stays stale after an edit while the link `href` changes.

findings.title: Untrusted-attribute spec does not cover website_name
findings.body: The 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' example lists `website` but not `website_name`. That is why the restricted-viewer leak in user_serializer.rb:153 passes this suite. Add `website_name` to this list, and add a restricted-viewer example for the website-name case.

verification.reason: The untrusted-attributes list in the spec includes `website` but not `website_name`, so the spec does not catch the TL0/anonymous leak.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain and scheme-less branches have no coverage
findings.body: The three new examples exercise the same-host branch and the parent-domain branch of `website_name`. The sibling-subdomain branch (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144-146, e.g. www.example.com against forum.example.com) and the nil-host path (138-140) have no examples. Add one example for each.

verification.reason: The new examples stub hostnames `discourse.org`, `example.com` and `forums.example.com`. These exercise the different-domain, same-host and parent-domain branches. No example covers the sibling-subdomain branch at line 146, or a website with no scheme, where the host is nil (line 140).

findings.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive
findings.body: `website_host == discourse_host` (line 141) compares the host as the user typed it. `URI#host` does not normalize case, so `http://Example.com/user` on instance `example.com` takes the else branch and shows `Example.com` without the path. Downcasing both hosts before the comparison would match the intent of the same-domain branch. Confidence is medium because I did not run the code to confirm the Ruby URI behavior.

verification.reason: The code compares `URI(website).host` with `Discourse.current_hostname` using plain `==` and `ends_with?`, and never downcases either side. Ruby's URI parser keeps the case of the host as written, so `http://Example.com/user` on `example.com` falls into the else branch and the path is dropped.

contracts.action: Anonymous visitor loads a TL0 user's profile (JSON endpoint and HTML preload) and receives website_name
contracts.before_after: Before: website is hidden for restricted viewers through untrusted_attributes, so the header has no website label. After: include_website_name returns true whenever website is present, which bypasses that restriction.
contracts.visible_effect: The host and path of a TL0 user's website appear in the profile header for anonymous visitors.
contracts.failure_mode: The restriction on TL0 profile fields is bypassed silently. No error is raised.

contracts.action: Header label now reads model.website_name instead of the controller's websiteName computed from model.website
contracts.before_after: Before: the label was derived from model.website, so it changed as the user typed on the preferences page. After: the label is server-computed and changes only when findDetails reloads the user.
contracts.visible_effect: On the preferences page the label stays stale after the website is edited or saved, while the link href follows the new value.
contracts.failure_mode: No error is shown. The stale label remains until the user leaves the page and returns to the profile.

contracts.action: Route entry or browser Back to the profile loads website_name via findDetails
contracts.before_after: Before and after: afterModel calls findDetails on every entry, and the preloaded JSON is consumed once via PreloadStore.getAndRemove. website_name is refreshed on each entry, with the same behavior as before.
contracts.visible_effect: Re-entering the profile shows the current website label.
contracts.failure_mode: If findDetails rejects, the route redirects to /404 (pre-existing behavior, not introduced here).

contracts.action: Server computes website_name from an unparseable or scheme-less website
contracts.before_after: Before: the JS label used split('/')[2] and was hidden when no host was present. After: the server returns nil and the label is hidden. Behavior matches the previous one.
contracts.visible_effect: The label is hidden. The link still uses model.website.
contracts.failure_mode: The URI parse error is rescued and nil is returned without a log. UserUpdater prefixes http:// on save, so this only happens for malformed stored values.

summary: The pull request moves the profile website label from a controller computed property to a server-computed `website_name` attribute. I reviewed all five files in this part. The change has one blocker: `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes`, and the explicit `include_website_name` overrides the restriction, so anonymous visitors see a TL0 user's website host and path. There is also a fix-level stale-label bug on the preferences page, where the label does not follow website edits or saves. Two tests are weak (the untrusted list omits `website_name`, and the new branches are not covered), and one case-sensitivity issue is a consider. The `websiteName` removal in the controller and the `profileBackground` doc correction are clean. No docs/adr files exist in the snapshot, so there was no ADR to check.
